summary: Notifications system has critical blockers preventing approval. Both reviewers confirm missing domain-event integration, identity resolution failures in controllers, lack of durable delivery/retry, authentication gaps, and incomplete test coverage. Plan items 1-15 are foundational; 16+ are blocked waiting for event emission confirmation from AuctionsModule.

consolidatedFindings.title: Domain event triggers are absent
consolidatedFindings.description: No requested auction, break, conclusion, or subscription event invokes NotificationService. Neither reviewer found @OnEvent listeners, EventEmitter2.emit calls, or direct invocations from accepted bids, settlement, break transitions, or subscription processing. EventEmitterModule.forRoot() registers a bus with no publishers or subscribers.
consolidatedFindings.impact: Notifications cannot be produced in normal operation; the entire dispatch pathway is dead code.
consolidatedFindings.remediation: Coordinate with AuctionsModule and SubscriptionsModule to emit post-commit events (bid.accepted, break.started, break.ended, auction.ended, subscription.expiring). NotificationService subscribes via @OnEvent handlers and resolves recipients from authoritative state. Add scheduled subscription-expiry producer.

consolidatedFindings.title: Prisma composition and migration drift
consolidatedFindings.description: build-schema.mjs does not include the duplicate Phase N schema (notifications.prisma). The composed identity schema still has only IN_APP and EMAIL, no SMS or profile phone. The migration adds SMS, phoneNumber, and delivery timestamps, but the schema file lacks all three. Schema validation passes only because the new file is excluded from composition.
consolidatedFindings.impact: Generated Prisma client lacks the new SMS enum, phoneNumber field, and retry-timestamp contract. Services will reference undefined fields, causing runtime failures.
consolidatedFindings.remediation: Update existing identity/support domain models (stop duplicating), create a matching migration covering all three changes, regenerate the Prisma client, and validate the actual pre-migration schema path.

consolidatedFindings.title: Authenticated identity is still invalid in controllers
consolidatedFindings.description: @CurrentUser('sub') returns the entire JWT payload, not a string. Cognito sub is not the internal User.id UUID. Controllers hardcode userId as 'user-id-from-jwt' placeholder; no @UseGuards(JwtGuard) is applied. All endpoints are publicly accessible.
consolidatedFindings.impact: Endpoints are unauthenticated and exposed. Even after wiring JWT, extracted identity will be wrong type for UUID-scoped queries (User lookups fail, cross-user access undetected).
consolidatedFindings.remediation: Apply @UseGuards(JwtGuard) to all controllers. Inject @CurrentUser(), extract sub from JWT, resolve User.id via UserIdentity.getCognitoIdByUserId(), pass internal UUID to all Prisma queries. Verify user owns notification before read/delete (403 FORBIDDEN if mismatch).

consolidatedFindings.title: Browser route and auth contracts do not match Nest API
consolidatedFindings.description: Frontend hooks call relative /api/v1/notifications URLs with credentials: 'include' (cookies). JwtGuard expects bearer tokens; the shared Axios client adds Authorization: Bearer. Next has no matching API route or rewrite for /api/v1. Nest also enables URI versioning with default 1, while controllers embed v1 without VERSION_NEUTRAL.
consolidatedFindings.impact: Frontend requests fail with 404 or auth rejection. Requests that reach the API are rejected because bearer token is missing.
consolidatedFindings.remediation: Declare one route version (URI or header-based). Use documented proxy or shared authenticated API client. Ensure Next API routes are configured to forward to Nest, or use VERSION_NEUTRAL on manually versioned controllers to unify the versioning strategy.

consolidatedFindings.title: Preference semantics are inconsistent and incomplete
consolidatedFindings.description: Disabling in-app does not remove a notification from the feed; it still appears after disabling. Omitted update fields reset other channels (omitted values become inApp: true, email: false, sms: false). Writes can partially apply via three sequential upserts. Consent timestamps are manufactured without validated evidence. SUBSCRIPTION_EXPIRING skips consent validation entirely.
consolidatedFindings.impact: User preferences don't control visibility. Preference changes are silent or stale. Marketing opt-ins don't require explicit user action, violating GDPR/CASL.
consolidatedFindings.remediation: Preserve omitted values in updates (only change specified channels). Use atomic transaction for all three upsert operations. Make feed visibility and consent follow stored preference choice. Record consentedAt only from defined user action with disclosure (not auto-manufactured). Add backend consent validation for marketing categories.

consolidatedFindings.title: Delivery is neither durable nor retried
consolidatedFindings.description: Persistence is deferred in-process via setImmediate. Pending rows have no consumer; getPendingDeliveries and incrementAttempts have no callers. Attempts stay zero. Transient provider failures are terminal; a rate-limited SMS never retries; SMS adapter marks PENDING, but no job ever processes PENDING records. Process exit loses the entire intent.
consolidatedFindings.impact: Failed email/SMS sends are permanent. Rate-limited SMS never recovers. High transient failure surface with zero retry mechanism.
consolidatedFindings.remediation: Use transactional outbox or durable queue with claimed jobs, backoff, and retryable vs terminal states. Implement background retry job consuming pending deliveries every 5 minutes with exponential backoff (max 3 attempts, then mark FAILED). Or defer retry to Phase N.3 and document as deferred.

consolidatedFindings.title: Idempotency compares the wrong key
consolidatedFindings.description: Idempotency check runs only when both auctionId and playerId exist; skips non-player events (break, subscription). Different players can suppress one another via shared auctionId. Compares only user, category, time, and data.auctionId (missing playerId in comparison). Top-level IDs are not merged into persisted data. No unique constraint enforces deduplication atomically.
consolidatedFindings.impact: SUBSCRIPTION_EXPIRING and other non-auction events can be duplicated. Rapid sequential bids from different players can suppress each other's notifications.
consolidatedFindings.remediation: Persist a stable source-event key (e.g., event source + timestamp + actor + subject). Insert under database uniqueness constraint (UNIQUE(userId, eventKey)). Verify constraint at database level, not application logic.

consolidatedFindings.title: History and badge represent only the first slice
consolidatedFindings.description: useNotifications hardcodes page=1, discards pagination metadata, exposes no page or category input. Account page filters first 20 rows locally (no pagination controls). Bell badge counts only 5 rows (9+ state unreachable). Unread count calculation is O(n) filter on every hook render (100+ notifications cause re-render overhead).
consolidatedFindings.impact: Older unread records disappear from view. Users cannot navigate notification history. Unread count is stale or missing. Frontend performance degrades with 100+ notifications.
consolidatedFindings.remediation: Return authoritative unread total from backend. Use server-driven pagination/category state. Memoize unreadCount or compute once in backend list response. Add pagination controls and category filter UI.

consolidatedFindings.title: Account screens miss shell, mobile, and keyboard behavior
consolidatedFindings.description: Pages Router screens live under src/pages; they do not inherit App Router shell (header, footer, global styles, AuthProvider). No Pages Router _app.tsx. Clickable divs have no keyboard behavior (no role, no onKeyDown). Switches have no accessible names or checked state. Dropdown doesn't manage focus. Badge motion ignores prefers-reduced-motion. Fixed multi-column layouts have no 375px alternative.
consolidatedFindings.impact: Notifications pages are unstyled (no header/footer). Keyboard users cannot interact. Screen reader users get no semantics. Mobile (375px) has no responsive layout.
consolidatedFindings.remediation: Move routes into App Router shell (/app/account/notifications, /app/account/settings/notifications). Add semantic HTML (button, switch, aria-label, role). Implement focus management for dropdown. Respect prefers-reduced-motion. Add responsive 375px card layout. Test with keyboard and screen reader.

consolidatedFindings.title: Provider output leaks PII and does not fail closed
consolidatedFindings.description: Success and invalid-recipient logs include full email addresses and phone numbers. Email HTML interpolates emailBody without escaping (markup can enter if notification text contains < > or &). Twilio defaults the sender to +1234567890 when TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER is unset (silent degradation, no configuration failure).
consolidatedFindings.impact: PII exposed in logs. HTML injection possible if notification body contains user-supplied data. SMS sent from placeholder number (users confused about source). Missing credentials silently degrade instead of failing closed.
consolidatedFindings.remediation: Redact email/phone identifiers in logs (log count or hash instead). Escape HTML interpolations or send plain text only. Require TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER to be configured and validated; fail startup if unset and SMS enabled. Validate SENDGRID_API_KEY at startup too.

consolidatedFindings.title: Test and build claims are unsupported
consolidatedFindings.description: Backend test file contains only placeholder.spec.ts with expect(true).toBe(true). Frontend has no notification-specific tests. No behavioral test suite for channels, delivery retry, rate limiting, preferences, or workflows. API typecheck reports notification-specific Prisma delegate/field errors (schema drift). Web typecheck passes only after worktree added missing date-fns dependency.
consolidatedFindings.impact: No coverage of core logic. Build will fail on missing dependencies (date-fns locked to worktree). Confidence is zero.
consolidatedFindings.remediation: Add 85+ unit tests covering notification dispatch, idempotency, channel resolution, adapter behavior (mocked), rate limiting, preference CRUD. Add integration tests for database persistence and authorization. Add E2E tests for auction workflow. Fix Prisma schema drift so API typecheck passes without workarounds. Remove worktree dependency lock.

consolidatedFindings.title: Phase N is bundled with unrelated phases and artifacts
consolidatedFindings.description: Commits include payments, squad exports, contracts, subscription changes, generated artifacts, planning documents, temporary review output, and earlier Phases J, K, L work. The branch range cannot be reviewed in isolation. Test run is against a dirty worktree with locked dependencies.
consolidatedFindings.impact: Cannot bisect, review, deploy, or revert Phase N independently. Git history is polluted. CI runs against mixed work.
consolidatedFindings.remediation: Split or restack Phase N notifications work onto its own migration and dependency set. Clean up generated artifacts and planning files. Rebase to include only notification service, controllers, frontend, and tests. Push clean commit history.

consolidatedFindings.title: SMS rate limit is global per-user, not per-auction; semantic unclear
consolidatedFindings.description: Redis counter key sms:rate-limit:{userId} is incremented regardless of category or auction. Once user hits 1 SMS per 5-minute window, next SMS is deferred (marked PENDING) regardless of event type or room. If user is host of two auctions and wins a bid in each within 5 minutes, only one SMS generates.
consolidatedFindings.impact: User may miss time-sensitive bid notifications if they've already received an SMS in the same window for a different auction.
consolidatedFindings.remediation: Clarify intent with product: is this spam prevention (acceptable) or should limits be per-category or per-auction? If per-design, document the trade-off clearly for users. If not, refactor rate limit key to include category or auctionId.

consolidatedFindings.title: Race condition: preference changes during dispatch
consolidatedFindings.description: resolveEnabledChannels is called once at dispatch start and not re-checked during adapter execution. If user disables email while BID_WON event is being processed, dispatch may still send email (window: 0–5 seconds of adapter execution).
consolidatedFindings.impact: User preference change takes 0–5 seconds to take effect. Edge case but technically observable.
consolidatedFindings.remediation: Acceptable for notification system (eventual consistency is fine). Document or monitor if needed. Alternative: re-check preferences per adapter before sending, but adds latency.

reviewerAgreement.summary: Both reviewers agree on 7 BLOCKER findings: missing domain-event integration, Prisma composition drift, invalid identity resolution, non-durable delivery with no retry, incomplete authentication, unsupported test claims, and bundled unrelated work. Disagreements are minor (Fable flags SMS rate-limit semantics as MEDIUM; GPT treats as lower priority). Overall consensus: NEEDS_CHANGES.

nextSteps: STOP implementation at plan item 15. Do NOT proceed to event listeners (item 17) until AuctionsModule event emission is confirmed.
Coordinate with AuctionsModule team: verify EventEmitter2 is wired and events (bid.accepted, break.started, etc.) are emitted post-commit. Item 16 is a BLOCKER checkpoint.
Fix authentication immediately: apply @UseGuards(JwtGuard), inject @CurrentUser(), resolve User.id via UserIdentity lookup. Item 3 must be resolved before shipping.
Fix Prisma schema composition: include notifications.prisma in build-schema.mjs or relocate models to identity/support domains. Regenerate client and migrations.
Implement durable delivery with retry: either transactional outbox or durable queue pattern. No fire-and-forget without recovery.
Add test coverage: unit tests for services (80%+), integration tests for endpoints and authorization, E2E tests for auction workflows.
Split Phase N work: remove payments, squad exports, contracts, and other unrelated commits. Push clean notification-only branch.
Re-run code review after fixes are applied.
